guide.summary: Customer-instance OAuth, admin registers client (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Public ServiceNow Store listing (approval path unconfirmed, wait 3-5 weeks). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Customer-instance OAuth, admin registers client (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none).

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you create an auth config with a client ID and secret from the customer's instance.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio offers no managed app for ServiceNow, and the client ID and secret come from an Application Registry record in each customer's instance.
reasons: No managed app exists in Composio for ServiceNow
Client credentials are generated per instance, not by a central ServiceNow portal
Managed apps would show Composio branding on the consent screen

scenarios.label: Customer-instance OAuth, admin registers client
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects to customers' own ServiceNow instances; no Store listing.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; relies on a customer admin acting

waiting.basis: The docs describe no provider review; the wait is on each customer's admin, which is not documented.

scenarios.approval: No ServiceNow review found. Each customer's admin must create the OAuth client in their instance.
extras: Admin registers OAuth client in each instance
gate_sequence: Customer admin creates OAuth record in Application Registry

modifiers.note: Admin registers OAuth client in each instance

scenarios.label: Public ServiceNow Store listing
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want to list your app on the ServiceNow Store for customers to find.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; partner enrollment and certification prep

waiting.basis: c15 (certification guide); c16 reports 1-2 days to 7 days (forum report)

scenarios.approval: Build Partner membership is required to list, followed by Store certification. Recertification can recur.

prerequisites.title: Admin access on the target instance
prerequisites.detail: Managing OAuth needs the security_admin role. Creating a JWT endpoint needs the admin role.

prerequisites.title: Trusted TLS certificate on the instance
prerequisites.detail: The OAuth client does not connect to endpoints with self-signed certificates.

prerequisites.title: Build Partner Program membership
prerequisites.detail: You must be a Build Partner to list on the Store. An Access level exists with fewer requirements, but the page gives no thresholds.

steps.title: Get a customer instance and admin contact
steps.detail: Find the customer admin, or your own test instance admin, who can open System OAuth > Application Registry.
steps.done_when: An admin is ready to create the OAuth record.

steps.title: Draft admin setup instructions
steps.detail: Write a short guide for the admin: create the OAuth client record, set the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard, and note the scopes you need.
steps.done_when: The admin has a clear checklist.

steps.title: Admin creates client and shares credentials
steps.detail: The admin creates the record. The client ID is auto-generated, and the secret can be auto-generated by leaving it empty. Share both securely.
steps.done_when: You hold the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config for the servicenow toolkit through Composio's API with the customer's client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Test the first connection
steps.detail: A user signs in once to fetch a token. Token requests must use form-encoded content, not JSON.

steps.title: Apply to the Build Partner Program
steps.detail: Submit the company and business details to join the partner program.

steps.title: Self-check against common certification failures
steps.detail: Review the app for UI actions with no condition, missing ACLs and other known failed checks.

steps.title: Store certification review
steps.detail: ServiceNow certifies the app. Plan for weeks; revalidation after releases can be faster.
steps.done_when: The app is ready for publishing.

traps.title: No central app to register
traps.detail: Each instance issues its own client credentials, so credentials differ per customer. Plan an onboarding step for every customer.

traps.title: JSON token requests fail unclearly
traps.detail: Token requests with application/json return an unspecified error. Use application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

traps.title: Self-signed certificates are rejected
traps.detail: Instances with self-signed certificates will not work with the OAuth client.

traps.title: Store apps must be recertified
traps.detail: Apps must stay within three releases of current, so expect recurring recertification about twice a year.

blockers.symptom: Admin cannot find or create the OAuth record
blockers.what_it_means: The user lacks the required role on the instance.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask for the security_admin role, or have a user with it create the record.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the role request and setup instructions.

blockers.symptom: Cannot list app on the Store
blockers.what_it_means: Build Partner membership comes before Store certification.
blockers.what_to_do: Join the Build Partner Program first.

evidence.quote: In addition to the initial certification, ServiceNow Store apps can require recertification.
evidence.answer: Reviews repeat: Store apps can require recertification beyond the initial certification, for new ServiceNow releases and code changes (per the same guide). No fixed yearly cycle or waiver was found.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The former, 1-2 days. Full reviews I've seen taken up to 7 days depending on what checks are required
evidence.answer: A community forum reply (Kieran Anson, Kilo Patron) reports 1-2 days for a family release revalidation with no code change, and up to 7 days for full reviews.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: UI Actions with an empty condition field can be called by any logged-in user.
evidence.answer: ServiceNow's certification team lists its most common failed checks; examples include UI actions with no condition, missing ACLs, and a missing contact support module.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Note that you must be a Build Partner to list an application on the ServiceNow Store.
evidence.answer: Build Partner Program membership is a gate before an app can be listed on the Store, so partner acceptance comes before certification.
